result:
Parking the roadmap. Stage 1 is the one shipped piece. Stage 2 and the three Ranked-list items go to the deferred backlog, and the roadmap retires as parked. Here are the calls in order.

**1. Read the schema and the existing backlog first**

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md   # Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                         # may not exist yet; append, never overwrite
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`**

There will be one item for each unticked stage and each Ranked-list item, under a dated section. Here is a draft. I'll match the field names to the schema once I've read it.

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure email notices to boat operators (from lock-closures-roadmap Stage 2, Track B)
      Boat operators get an email within an hour of a lock closing, from a job that polls the closure log's live feed about every 10 minutes and sends to an operator mailing list. Text-message notices were never in scope.
      Size: small (one closure-log poll each 10 minutes)
      Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (from lock-closures-roadmap Ranked list A, O2)
      A daily 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock, built from the river-level forecast. It uses the closure-vs-gauge curve in specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md: closures are under 2% of days below 3.1 m and about 60% at 3.8 m.
      Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop)
      Done when: a 7-day outlook for each lock is produced from the real forecast, and a findings file records the result and the measured cost of the real run.

- [ ] Pooled per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks (from lock-closures-roadmap Ranked list A, O3)
      Separate closure-vs-gauge curves for each of the 14 locks, pooled across locks. Stage 1 found the four longest-record locks show close to the same curve.
      Size: large (about 14 times Stage 1's data; Stage 1 was 1.8 GB / 22 min)
      Done when: per-lock curves for all 14 locks are fit on real data, and a findings file records them and the measured cost of the real run.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (from lock-closures-roadmap Ranked list A, O4)
      A static map page showing each lock's closure history, for the canal's boat operators.
      Size: about a day of work (one static map page)
      Done when: the map page shows closure history for every lock from the real closure log.
```

**3. Retire the roadmap as parked**

```
mkdir -p specs/completed
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Edit specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md   # add under the title:
    > PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Canal study funding ended; remaining work is in specs/deferred_items.md under "lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06".
```

There is no methodology or critique file to retire with it, because this roadmap had no spec. The Stage 1 findings file stays where it is, since the deferred items cite it.

**4. Commit locally on `main`**

```
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete): funding ended; defer Stage 2 and Ranked list A"
```

I won't push.

After this, nothing is live. The four items will age in the deferred backlog and come up through `/deferred` if the work is ever picked up again. Stage 2's email notices don't depend on the study's results. If anyone still wants them without the study, that one item can be promoted on its own.
